raw_case_text: In July 2013, 53-year-old male, Caucasian, unemployed, from Mundo Novo, State of Bahia, Brazil, attended to the Stomatology Clinic at University Hospital, presenting with pain, nasal obstruction, and complaints of odynophagia and dysphagia. Physical examination showed painful, hyperemic and friable lesion in the right nasal cavity, associated with infiltrative lesion on the hard and soft palate, and uvula ( Figure 1c). We observed ulcerated lesion on the left eyebrow and right eye with seropurulent secretion, a small ulcer on the lower eyelid, on the lobe of the right ear and a lesion in the malar region. The patient was admitted for diagnosis and treatment of disseminated skin lesions. A biopsy of the palate lesions revealed a non-specific erosive chronic inflammatory process. The patient was HIV negative and positive for Montenegro reaction. Treatment with amphotericin B was initiated at a dose of 150 mg/d up to a maximum dose of 2,410 mg. Lesions regressed after drug treatment and oral treatment was initiated during hospitalization. We removed dental foci without any intercurrence. One month later, the patient was discharged. However, in August 2013, in outpatient medical consultation, the lesions were observed in nasal mucosa and palate. He was followed up in the outpatient clinic and treatment with glucantime 20 mg/kg/day was prescribed for one month. The follow-up period was eight months, and the result was negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 53-year-old Caucasian male from Mundo Novo, Bahia, Brazil, presented in July 2013 with painful nasal obstruction, odynophagia, dysphagia, invasive palatal/uvular/nasal mucosal lesions, and multifocal facial and periocular ulcers.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the University Hospital Stomatology Clinic in July 2013 with painful nasal and oropharyngeal mucosal lesions alongside multiple facial and periocular ulcers, experienced initial regression with amphotericin B (2,410 mg cumulative dose), and developed recurrent nasal mucosal and palatal lesions at his 1-month outpatient follow-up in August 2013.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unemployed Caucasian male from Mundo Novo, State of Bahia, Brazil; HIV-negative.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for nasal pain, nasal obstruction, odynophagia, dysphagia, and facial/ocular ulceration.

objective.physical_examination: Painful, hyperemic, friable lesion in the right nasal cavity; infiltrative granulomatous lesion involving the hard palate, soft palate, and uvula; ulcerated lesions on the left eyebrow and right eye with seropurulent discharge; and smaller ulcers on the lower eyelid, right earlobe, and malar region.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV serology was negative, and the Montenegro intradermal test was positive.
objective.advanced_workup: Palatal mucosal biopsy demonstrated a nonspecific chronic erosive inflammatory infiltrate.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Positive Montenegro intradermal reaction and characteristic disseminated mucocutaneous and periocular ulcers (with HIV excluded) confirmed Disseminated American Tegumentary (Mucocutaneous) Leishmaniasis. Following initial inpatient intravenous amphotericin B (150 mg/day to a cumulative dose of 2,410 mg) and dental focus removal, an early mucosal relapse in August 2013 was treated with systemic meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime 20 mg/kg/day for 1 month), achieving complete remission over 8 months of follow-up.
